newsitem.title: USA: Conseco buying Colonial Penn Life.
newsitem.headline: Conseco buying Colonial Penn Life.

text.p: Conseco Inc., which has acquired more than 40 insurance companies, Wednesday agreed to buy Colonial Penn Life Insurance Co. from Leucadia National Corp. for $460 million, giving it a new channel for selling its products.
Colonial Penn, probably best known for its television commercials featuring former "Tonight Show" sidekick Ed McMahon, sells life insurance to older people.

The acquisition will give Conseco, a Carmel, Ind.-based financial services company, the chance to sell its products using Colonial Penn's TV commercials, direct mail and telemarketing, Conseco Chairman Stephen Hilbert said in an interview.

Conseco also reported record first-quarter operating profit of $119.1 million that slightly exceeded Wall Street analysts' expectations. The company attributed the good results to sales and acquistions.
Although Conseco has a broad distribution system, using both company and independent agents, Hilbert said the company has not used direct marketing to sell its products.
"The one distribution point that we have been aggressively looking for is the right direct marketing company," Hilbert said.
"This is going to give us, again, an opportunity to hit the public and to target our markets as far as which segment of the buying public we want to target," he said.
Hilbert said he plans to sell Conseco's supplemental health, life, annuity and mutual fund products through Colonial Penn.
He also said he plans to allow Colonial Penn to continue operating as it does now in Philadelphia rather than absorbing it into Conseco. He said he does not foresee much cost cutting.

The acquisition, for cash and notes, is subject to approval by regulators, and is expected to close in the third quarter, Conseco said. It said the transaction is expected to modestly increase operating profits in 1997 and 1998.

Conseco's $115.1 million in first-quarter net income more than doubled the $46.3 million it earned a year earlier. The earning equalled 49 cents a share, up from 39 cents a share a year earlier, as revenue grew to $1.10 billion fromn $692 million.

The operating earnings of $119.1 million, or 59 cents a share, compared with $48.4 million, or 44 cents a share, a year earlier. Analysts on average had predicted operating earnings of 58 cents a share.

New York-based Leucadia said the Colonial Penn Life deal would produce a pretax gain of $300 million, and that it remained in talks for sale of its other life and property-casualty insurance operations.
Conseco, one of the most acquisitive U.S. life insurance companies, said it will continue to look for more acquisitions and has the finances to pursue deals as large as $2 billion.
Conseco has completed 16 transactions involving more than 40 insurance companies since 1982. Its acquisition of Pioneer Financial Services is expected to close by the end of May.
Conseco stock ended unchanged at $41.375 and Leucadia rose 75 cents to $30.375, both in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
